sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton featuring a mostly complete skull, lower jaws, and the front portion of the postcranial skeleton.
This large theropod possessed a skull measuring 75 to 80 cm and a total body length estimated at 7 to 8 meters.
Its premaxillary teeth displayed large serrations on the rear edge but only tiny serrations on the front edge.
The name Asfaltovenator translates to "Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter," referencing the specific geological layer where its fossils were discovered.
Preparing the fossil took five years because the stone matrix surrounding it was extremely hard.
A technician named Leandro Canesa discovered the Asfaltovenator skeleton in 2002 near Cerro Condor.
Oliver Rauhut and Diego Pol formally named and described the species Asfaltovenator vialidadi in 2019.
Fossils of Asfaltovenator were found in the Chacritas Member, which consists of lake and river deposits.
The lake environment where Asfaltovenator lived, known as the Chacritas Paleolake, was likely shallow, saline, or hypersaline.

Phylogenetic analysis recovered Asfaltovenator as the most basal allosauroid and Megalosauroidea as a paraphyletic grade leading to Allosauroidea due to its mosaic of primitive and derived characters within Tetanurae.
The genus Asfaltovenator belongs to the parent group Allosauroidea.
Asfaltovenator lived during the Middle Toarcian of the Lower Jurassic in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina.
The animal lived between 180.4 and 168.6 million years ago during the Toarcian to Bajocian stages.
In 2024, Andrea Cau proposed that Asfaltovenator belongs within Megalosauroidea as a sister taxon to Sciurumimus or within a larger stem group.
